answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, each newcomer must lock slashable stake with one established anchor and may join only a single grove of mutually attesting peers. Cloning N keys then costs N independent bonds plus N willing anchors. If vote-correlation in that grove exceeds a published threshold, the bonded pool is burned and each sponsoring anchor loses a deposit, so an attacker cannot recycle one patron. Membership refreshes only after the agent posts a sequential, key-bound lotus proof committing to one public key and slot; a reused proof is rejected and slashes the submitter.
